checks.reason: One available terminal bit pays Delta_sched once, before separately bounding the two ideal-game event probabilities.
G_leaf supplies independent keys; the proposition restricts confirmation keys to the declared services.
The existing multiple-message classical row lemma, with quantum ordinary oracle access, applies; the immutable report-row lemma is not substituted.
T_d includes construction and verification digest evaluations after exact-input caching.
V_d counts repeated attempts separately; one cached digest can have many candidate tags.
B_c includes complete outside work; remaining real rows cost at most four h calls per distinct 32-byte HMAC evaluation.
The forced-rejection game has no secret W-dependent reply on unissued messages; the identical-state prefix coupling justifies V/2^256.
The stopping point is the first internal MAC equality, before later persistence or public-response outcomes.
A new core with an issued same-role digest yields two distinct length-framed H inputs, requiring collision rather than preimage security.
Directly read published Zhandry Theorem 7, printed page 562; the final text uses C(q+2)^3/N and the corresponding journal URL.
All ordinary/honest H calls, preparation and terminal testing are counted; independent h and private tables are ancillary operations.
Honest first private construction creates the origin; expected-tag verification never converts a guess into an issued tag.
Retained cores and alternative signatures retain their original construction entry; accidental numeric key coincidences remain in the shared-oracle comparisons.
One original selected encryption plus all classical selected decryptions is the exact declared integrity interface; a new authenticated install implies a new valid decryption pair.
First private computation precedes release/commit; exact Resume returns the same original send result and consumes no second challenge encryption.
Pinned send_input checks pending ID/plaintext/ad; resume_message offers no replacement payload or new message ID.
Pinned Traffic::receive decrypts before Incoming insertion; DeviceJournal persists a fresh entry before returning plaintext.
